space.name: Public Organization Space
space.description: Organizations wielding delegated public authority under law: ministries, councils, delivery and research bodies, task groups, arm's-length agencies, state-owned enterprises, municipalities, and public-private hybrids.

universe.description: Public organizations wielding delegated public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under any basis of authority - constitutional, statutory, customary, religious, dynastic, party, military, colonial, or treaty.
excludes: informal groups without a constituting order

meta.description: Four comparative representation systems for comparing public organizations across polities and periods: ontological, functional, purpose-driven, and model-derived.

systems.name: ontological
systems.title: Ontological Set
systems.description: Profiles what public bodies are: their legal standing, institutional kind, composition, resources, permanence, and spatial definition. Derived by ontological analysis - enumerating the entities, kinds, and modes of existence the domain contains. Use it to compare bodies as entities before asking what they do or how they relate.
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the organization decomposition and agency-form comparison
systems.universe: Bodies exercising or asserting public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under any basis of authority - constitutional, statutory, customary, religious, dynastic, party, military, colonial, or treaty.
systems.purpose: Compare what bodies are: existence, kind, composition, and permanence.

elements.name: Institutional Standing
elements.description: Whether the body holds legal personality, is a dependent public body, or is an office without personhood.
elements.assignment_rule: Code independent where it owns property and litigates in its own name; dependent where it is a distinct public body lacking full personhood; office where the holder, not the body, holds the legal position.

elements.name: Organizational Form
elements.description: The recognized kind of public body.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by charter and function jointly; hybrids take public-private hybrid only under mixed control; bodies chartered by more than one polity take supranational body.

elements.name: Recruitment Mode
elements.description: The dominant mode by which members or post-holders are installed.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the mode filling the majority of the deciding membership; no majority mode takes mixed.

elements.name: Office Maintenance
elements.description: How the post-holder is materially sustained.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the dominant material basis of the office; salaried posts take salary; unpaid honorific posts take none.

elements.name: Resource Base
elements.description: The largest class of resources the body commands.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the dominant resource of the body's operation; bodies without holdings take none.

elements.name: Financing Mode
elements.description: The revenue base financing the body's operation.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the largest revenue share over the body's operating period.

elements.name: Authority Basis
elements.description: The basis on which the body's authority rests.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the highest basis claimed for the body's authority; bodies removable by decree take executive decree.

elements.name: Permanence
elements.description: How permanently the body is constituted.
elements.assignment_rule: Read the constituting order: a dissolution clause gives task-bound; a renewal term gives renewable mandate; otherwise permanent. The basis of permanence is coded under Authority Basis.

elements.name: Jurisdictional Extent
elements.description: The scale at which the body's authority runs.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the polity that charters it and the reach of its remit, not by where it operates.

elements.name: Territorial Basis
elements.description: Whether authority runs over people, land, function, or beyond territory.
elements.assignment_rule: Code personal where the remit follows persons (kin, estate, community); territorial where it follows bounded land.

elements.name: Mandate Scope
elements.description: How wide the constituting remit runs.
elements.assignment_rule: Count the domains named in the constituting order, not those grown by practice.

systems.name: functional
systems.title: Functional Set
systems.description: Profiles what public bodies do: the task families they perform, coded by exercised activity rather than charter rhetoric. Derived by functional analysis - enumerating the functions and activities of the domain. Use it to compare workloads and task portfolios across bodies with different legal forms.
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the function taxonomy and agency mandates
systems.universe: Bodies exercising or asserting public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under any basis of authority - constitutional, statutory, customary, religious, dynastic, party, military, colonial, or treaty.
systems.purpose: Compare what bodies do: task families by exercised activity.

elements.name: Service & Provision
elements.description: Whether the body delivers services, protection, or provision to end users.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the dominant provision; commissioned where it funds or compels others to deliver; none for bodies that only rule or extract.

elements.name: Regulation
elements.description: Whether the body forms binding rules, licenses, or authoritative counsel.
elements.assignment_rule: Code rule-making where it issues binding rules in its own right; licensing where its only binding act is granting or refusing permissions; advisory where it only counsels; none otherwise.

elements.name: Enforcement
elements.description: Whether the body compels compliance.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the highest exercised in its operating period; inspection without sanction stays inspection.

elements.name: Adjudication
elements.description: Whether the body decides individual cases with binding effect.
elements.assignment_rule: Code binding only where decisions are enforceable without further approval.

elements.name: Resource Extraction
elements.description: Whether the body draws resources from the population.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the dominant mode by which it draws resources; bodies that only spend take none.

elements.name: Knowledge and Record
elements.description: Whether the body produces knowledge, records, or evidence.
elements.assignment_rule: Code in-house where dedicated staff produce it on establishment; religious where the knowledge is sacral.

elements.name: Ritual / Ideological Administration
elements.description: Whether the body carries sacral, ritual, or ideological functions.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the dominant sacral or ideological function exercised; secular bodies take none.

elements.name: Military Mobilization
elements.description: Whether the body raises, commands, or supplies force.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the dominant military function; bodies with no force function take none.

elements.name: Representation
elements.description: Whether the body aggregates estates, communities, or constituencies.
elements.assignment_rule: Code where the body's dominant function is to voice or aggregate constituencies.

elements.name: Coordination & Oversight
elements.description: Whether the body coordinates or supervises other bodies.
elements.assignment_rule: Code lead coordinator where it convenes and sets the agenda of a standing coordination arrangement; supervisory only with a formal oversight mandate over named bodies.

elements.name: Commercial Operation
elements.description: Whether the body operates commercially or by trading monopoly.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the pricing rule of its trading activity; bodies with no trading activity take none.

elements.name: Emergency Powers
elements.description: Whether the body holds extraordinary powers.
elements.assignment_rule: Code standing where powers are exercisable without fresh authorization.

systems.name: purpose-driven
systems.title: Purpose-Driven Set
systems.description: Profiles what decision-makers need to know: answerability, changeability, rationalization, centralization, embeddedness, fidelity of performance signals, and risk. Derived by purpose-driven analysis - starting from the questions, decisions, and analytical tasks the comparison must support, then selecting the elements that answer them. Use it when a decision, not a description, is the output.
systems.frame_basis: Purpose-driven analysis from canonical comparison questions
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the evaluation and governance questions
systems.universe: Bodies exercising or asserting public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under any basis of authority - constitutional, statutory, customary, religious, dynastic, party, military, colonial, or treaty.
systems.purpose: Answer decisions: answerability, changeability, rationalization, centralization, embeddedness, risk.

elements.name: Accountability Depth
elements.description: Whether answerability carries consequences.
elements.assignment_rule: Code full where a completed accountability cycle has removed or sanctioned leadership in the body's history or class.

elements.name: Changeability
elements.description: How the body can be reorganized or abolished.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the instrument or force needed for abolition in the body's order.

elements.name: Rationalization Degree
elements.description: How rational-legal the body's structure is against patrimonial, charismatic, and traditional types.
elements.assignment_rule: Code rational-legal where offices are defined by rules and merit; patrimonial where offices are personal and heritable; charismatic where authority attaches to a leader.

elements.name: Centralization
elements.description: How centralized decision-making is.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by where the decisive authority sits relative to the bulk of operations.

elements.name: Loss Bearer
elements.description: Who bears the financial or material residual loss.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by who absorbs a deficit or loss in practice, not in theory.

elements.name: Performance Visibility
elements.description: How observable the body's performance is to outsiders.
elements.assignment_rule: Code published with regularly released measures; inspection where external inspection exists; internal where measurement stays inside.

elements.name: Mandate Clarity
elements.description: How precisely the mandate states what success looks like.
elements.assignment_rule: Code from the constituting order, not from practice.

elements.name: Capture Exposure
elements.description: Exposure to capture by concentrated interests.
elements.assignment_rule: Code low with tenure protections plus transparency duties; high with revolving-door leadership or concentrated interests; medium otherwise.

elements.name: Patron-Client Position
elements.description: The body's position within patronage or faction networks.
elements.assignment_rule: Code central patron where it dispenses offices and largesse; autonomous where no such network binds it.

systems.name: model-derived
systems.title: Model-Derived Set
systems.description: Derives characteristic elements from an overarching model of the public organization: chartered authority made operable through mandate, principals, governance, agency, execution, resources, accountability, and ecology. Each submodel contributes its elements; together they form one comparative profile. The composite-model approach worked as a system.
systems.frame_basis: Composite-model approach: overarching Public Organization Model in eight submodels
systems.provenance: authored as a new model decomposition for this atlas
systems.universe: Bodies exercising or asserting public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under any basis of authority - constitutional, statutory, customary, religious, dynastic, party, military, colonial, or treaty.
systems.purpose: Full-model profiling: every submodel contributes elements to one profile.

elements.name: Constituting Form
elements.description: Charter submodel: the form of the constituting instrument or order.
elements.assignment_rule: Cite the constituting instrument or order.

elements.name: Mandate Scope
elements.description: Charter submodel: how wide the constituting remit runs.
elements.assignment_rule: Count the domains named in the constituting order, not those grown by practice.

elements.name: Political Principal
elements.description: Principal submodel: the authority answered to.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the authority that appoints, directs, or dismisses the leadership.

elements.name: Direction Instruments
elements.description: Principal submodel: the instruments carrying current objectives.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the instrument whose breach has consequences.

elements.name: Governing Structure
elements.description: Governance submodel: the arrangement deciding direction and whose signature settles a contested decision.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the body that can overrule the chief executive; where a contested decision is settled by an individual holder, code the matching single-leader form.

elements.name: Decision Procedure
elements.description: Agency submodel: how contested decisions are reached.
elements.assignment_rule: Test with a contested decision: what procedure settles it.

elements.name: Rule Mode
elements.description: Governance submodel: whether the body rules subjects directly or through intermediaries.
elements.assignment_rule: Code indirect where authority over subjects is exercised through notables, chiefs, or elites.

elements.name: Functions
elements.description: Execution submodel: the task family performed.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by mandate-weighted dominant family, using evidence where available.

elements.name: Operational Deployment
elements.description: Execution submodel: geographic distribution of activities.
elements.assignment_rule: Map where activities are performed, not where staff sit.

elements.name: Funding Regime
elements.description: Resource submodel: the revenue base.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the largest revenue share over the operating period.

elements.name: Personnel Regime
elements.description: Resource submodel: how people are employed and managed.
elements.assignment_rule: Code by the dominant installation and tenure mode.

elements.name: Accountability Line
elements.description: Accountability submodel: the monitoring arrangement with consequences.
elements.assignment_rule: Code the arrangement that can trigger leadership consequences.

elements.name: Ecclesiastical Relation
elements.description: Ecology submodel: how the body stands toward religious authority.
elements.assignment_rule: Code fused where religious and public authority are one; caesaropapist where the polity heads but does not fuse with religion.
